attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 9.2.24 (RHEL7 base channel) streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys). Verified live streaming replication, then exercised a full primary-loss failover: stopped node1, promoted node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss, repointed node3 to follow node2 (copying the new timeline history file since PG 9.2 can't fetch it over the replication stream), and rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 = writable primary, node1 and node3 = streaming standbys, all data (4 rows in repl_check) consistent across all three. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), confirming boot_id change and full replication/data recovery after each restart.
